Der von dem Kommerzienrat Hesselberger, Nürnberg, und Hans Edler von der Planitz, Christiania, unternommenen Jagdexpedition ( 1911 ) wurde es auf besonderes Ansuchen gestat- tet, je ein Exemplar des Vogels für die Zoologischen Sammlungen in Nürnberg und Christiania zu erlegen. An dem Vogel, der von einer Münchner Firma präpariert worden ist, fällt vor allem der unförmliche Schnebel auf, der dem Tier seinen Namen gibt.

Der Bart des Braunauer Ratsherrn HANS STEININGER in seiner jetzigen Gestalt befindet sich jetzt im Besitz der Stadt Braunau. Länge: 2,07 Meter.
This queer looking thing is a beard

which once belonged to a man named Hans Steininger, senator of the town of B$^{a}$aunau-on-Inn in Upper Austria, who died in 1567. The beard which is 2,07 meters, or 6 feet 9 inches long, was cut off the face of its owner after his death 345 years ago, and it has just been recovered by the town of Braunau after the strange relic has been, during all these centuries, partly in private possession, partly stowed away in a museum at Augsburg, Bavaria. Herr Steininger lies buried at the foot of the parish-Church in Braunau, and his tomb-stone, which is put in the church-wall, shows him in the adornment of his majestic beard for which it seems he has been known throughout the country. As the chronicle says, Herr Steininger met his death by his beard by stepping on it while ascending some stairs, He fell and was so fatally injured that he died. As a fact, the inhabitants of Braunau are very happy that they have finally got into their possession the relic which has so long been withheld from them.
